title: Length-adaptive window aggregator for padding reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Our serving runtime experiences significant token waste from conservative padding in the batcher when request length distribution is heavy-tailed. Current bucketing coalescers reduce waste but struggle when prefill and decode phases co-occur and when kernel selection preferences change per sequence length. Goal: introduce a length-adaptive window aggregator that groups in-flight requests into dynamic windows (variable-width, sliding) that trade a small, bounded latency increase for large padding savings and better kernel matches. The aggregator should be prefill-aware (prioritize prefill-prefixed coalescing), emit kernel-hint metadata for the scheduler, and expose a tunable latency cap per customer tier.
implementation_steps: Instrument current batcher to emit per-request sequence histograms and kernel-preference stats
Prototype a lightweight sliding-window classifier in the batcher that groups requests by (effective_remaining_tokens, prefill_flag, historical-kernel-hit)
Add kernel_hint header to packed request metadata and surface to kernel selection layer
Implement pad-elision pass that validates compatibility (same attention mask shape or compatible KV reuse)
Add telemetry counters: padded_tokens_saved, added_latency_p90, kernel_switch_rate
Integrate rollout flags and per-customer latency cap configuration in routing layer
End-to-end tests: perf harness with synthetic heavy-tail and conversational traffic, verify correctness with functional tests
acceptance_criteria: >= 22% reduction in padded tokens on heavy-tail synthetic workload at default config
p50 end-to-end latency increase <= 5ms and p95 increase <= 25ms compared to baseline for production traffic
No functional regressions: outputs identical for requests when pad-elision is disabled; tolerant differences when enabled must be within existing QA thresholds
Kernel selection hinting reduces kernel-switch events by >= 15% in the mixed-length benchmark
Feature gated with rollout controls and observability dashboards available in Console
test_plan: Microbench: per-kernel perf with and without aggregator for seq lengths 8..2048
Integration: perf harness with conversational traces from anonymized logs (internal dataset)
Correctness: Fuzz request pad/attention patterns, assert identical logits when pad-elision disabled
Canary rollout: deploy to dedicated small subset of users, monitor padded_tokens_saved, latency, error-rate for 48h
Benchmark against existing bucketing baseline used in ENG-4721 and ENG-62045
